items.title: Abeille Marengo Sails to Begin Greece-Cyprus Cable Surveys as Turkey Claims Its Consent Was Obtained, Athens Pushes Back
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - The French research vessel Abeille Marengo sailed from the port of Heraklion at 6:26 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, to begin seabed surveys for the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection. Hours later, Turkey issued a new NAVTEX concerning the vessel’s activities, claiming that the surveys had been coordinated with the competent Turkish authorities and that their consent had been obtained, prompting a response from Athens. The Abeille Marengo, which had arrived in Crete from Italy and remained at the port of Heraklion pending the start of operations, departed with the assistance of a tugboat after a pilot boarded the vessel. It is initially expected to calibrate its scientific equipment before beginning seabed mapping along the planned cable route, from the Korakia area of Heraklion to Cyprus. The work includes hydrographic and geotechnical surveys, seabed sampling, penetration tests, and drilling, using specialized equipment such as multibeam echosounders, side-scan sonar, and magnetometers.

items.title: US Soldier Arrested in UK Spy Probe
items.summary_raw:
British counter-terrorism police arrested a U.S. Army member near Gloucester on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia.

The 41-year-old is in custody at a London police station. He was detained under Sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act 2023.

Two properties in Gloucestershire are being searched. MI5, the FBI and the U.S. military are working the case with UK police.

Per BBC News and LBC.

As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.

Another 17,000 parts in maintenance or repair, worth $1.3 billion, never made it into the inventory system. That figure could reach $2.5 billion.

As of March 2026, over 1 million parts worth more than $85 million remained unaccounted for since GAO's 2023 report.

Government Accountability Office, Nov. 9

Jerusalem Post Report: Admiral Igor Kostyukov, chief of Russia's GRU military intelligence agency, made an unusual visit to Israel.

A Russian military transport aircraft carrying his senior delegation landed at Ben Gurion Airport Saturday evening. The group met senior Israeli defense officials. What they discussed remains unclear.

The plane left Monday for Abu Dhabi. The delegation will join the U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine negotiations there on November 10 and 11.

Stiell joined Cop31 hosts Turkey and Australia, which is leading the negotiations, in promoting renewable energy and a new electrification goal as an optimistic alternative to a planet still tied to oil, coal and gas.

items.title: Democrats to attend Cop31 climate talks boosted by midterms and eager to make up for Trump-era setbacks
items.summary_raw:
US government will have no official presence at UN’s annual climate summit, this year’s Cop31 held in Antalya, Turkey

The US will be absent from key UN climate talks that start on Monday, a further sign of Donald Trump’s scornful dismissal of the climate crisis. But Democrats’ crushing win in the US midterm elections has delivered a timely shot of optimism to countries now looking beyond the Trump era of climate obstruction.

For the second year in a row, there will be no official US government presence at the annual climate summit, this year known as Cop31 and held in Antalya, Turkey. While almost every other country in the world sends delegations to the talks, Trump has derided the climate crisis as a “hoax” and “bullshit” and triggered the withdrawal of the US from the entire international climate framework.

items.title: Democrats Plan to Push Clean Energy to Lower Bills and Challenge Trump’s Fossil Fuel Agenda
items.summary_raw:
Some Democrats are promising to push for more clean energy to help tackle rising energy costs when they take control of Congress in January, though President Donald Trump says he will use his veto power aggressively. With new majorities in the House and Senate after last week's midterms, Democrats can set an agenda boosting clean energy and addressing climate change. While those are traditionally core priorities of the party, climate was not a central topic in this election cycle. Democrats can begin investigations and hold hearings into climate policy rollbacks and elimination of green energy grants by the Republican administration, potentially trying to undo some changes and restore renewable energy incentives.

The post Democrats Plan to Push Clean Energy to Lower Bills and Challenge Trump’s Fossil Fuel Agenda appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Greece-Cyprus Cable Project Enters Its Most Critical Phase Yet
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – The Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection project is entering a critical phase, as Athens moves to restart surveys ahead of the laying of the submarine cable, while Turkey disputes Greek jurisdiction and warns of a possible escalation of tensions in the Eastern Mediterranean. The next decisive step is expected on November 9 or 10, when the French survey vessel Abeille Marengo is scheduled to depart from Heraklion and begin operations southeast of Karpathos, weather conditions permitting. The Greek government has already completed the necessary permitting procedures. On November 6, Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis signed the relevant decision, followed by the issuance of a Greek NAVTEX, valid until March 6, 2027.

The post Greece-Cyprus Cable Project Enters Its Most Critical Phase Yet appeared first on The National Herald.

High-stakes talks involving 190 countries begin on Monday as world grapples with El Niño supercharged by fossil fuels

The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can see is real”, its host has said as scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks.

The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the strongest El Niño weather system on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.

Trump administration has gutted regulations that protect lives and natural resources as pipeline build-out continues

Datacenters are spurring a boom in fossil fuel pipeline projects at a time when the Trump administration is gutting rules that protect from disasters along the lines, a new review of federal records shows.

The report, compiled by the Environmental Integrity Project, also found pipelines are being built to meet demand for natural gas exports fueled by wars in Ukraine and Iran. Federal records identified almost 200 pipeline projects that are proposed or in the works, and would collectively span 17,000 miles (27,000km).

items.title: Who’s who at Cop31: key players at the climate talks
items.summary_raw:
What are the relationships and dominant interests in play, as the summit kicks off after a bitter row over its hosting?

Hosting Cop was a key pledge from Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese in 2021, while in opposition, before his successful election campaign. But arcane rules meant the country had to wait its turn to bid and was then embroiled in an angry row with Turkey over the hosting. The final compromise put Australia in charge of the negotiations which will take place in the Turkish city of Antalya. The bitter taste left by the row lingers and Australia has seemed to some a rather half-hearted host. About 53 percent of Air Force aircraft are over 30 years old, and 55 percent have exceeded their projected service life. The Air Force has requested about $4.25 billion for parts supply in fiscal 2027.

items.title: New ‘high safety’ chemicals in plastic food packaging linked to lower birth weight, study finds
items.summary_raw:
Dinch, an allegedly ‘safe’ alternative, used in the EU and US also found to cause fetal development complications

Exposure to a new generation of allegedly “safe” plasticizers is linked to lower birth weight and fetal development complications, which could cause serious health problems later in life, a new peer-reviewed study found.

As the health risks in exposure to common phthalate plasticizers became clear over the last few decades, industry began switching to a new type of chemical, called Dinch, that it claimed was a “high safety”, nontoxic alternative. It is widely used in soft plastic food packaging in the United States and European Union, and is found in children’s toys, medical devices, some textiles, flooring and other consumer goods.

items.title: The Turkish Ruse: Smoke on the High Seas?
items.summary_raw:
Pay attention here please because this topic is a real MEGO – My Eyes Glaze Over – but it’s important to Greece, and Cyprus, and speaks to the doublespeak chicanery that is the modus operandi of Turkey. Apparently they don’t teach geography in Turkey either, at least not for politicians and officials who can’t read a map unless it’s the unreasonable facsimile of the Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean under the dubious Blue Homeland Doctrine. Under that, Turkey declares a vast maritime jurisdiction of roughly 178,379 square miles in those waters which are Greek. Turkey believes calling something by what it wants and staking a claim means the territory or waters are Turkish, even if they are not. Turkey also asserted rights to continental shelves and Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) near its coastline.

items.title: Morning update
items.summary_raw:
Morning update

Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:

*Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, has said that efforts at mediation between Iran and the United States remain active to prevent escalation, warning that the crisis "cannot be left unresolved".

*Qatar has denied reports that its prime minister said the United States and Iran had failed to reach an agreement to end the war, calling the claims “false and misleading”.

*US President Donald Trump says Washington had made considerable progress in its dealings with Iran, while acknowledging that US forces had carried out limited strikes against targets on the country.

*Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated

items.summary_raw:
US offers $20 million reward for info on Iran's nuclear programme

Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.

A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.

The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

items.title: Trump says 'there would be no Israel' if Iran was allowed nuclear weapon
items.summary_raw:
Trump says 'there would be no Israel' if Iran was allowed nuclear weapon

US President Donald Trump says Israel would no longer exist if he had allowed Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon, while defending his military campaign against Tehran.

Speaking at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday, Trump  said: “If I allowed Iran to have a nuclear weapon, today there would be no Israel,” he said.

“Israel would’ve been wiped off the face of the earth,” Trump added, according to Al Jazeera.

items.title: New Turkish NAVTEX for Underwater Studies for the Pipeline with the Pseudo-State
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA – Turkey issued a new NAVTEX from the Antalya station concerning scientific research and underwater studies to be conducted at 12 specified coordinates in the Mediterranean between October 26 and December 31, 2026, in the maritime area between Turkey and occupied Cyprus. According to the website of Turkish state television TRT, the studies will be carried out by the vessels R/V Denar Pathfinder, Denar Echo, Denar Explorer, and Kırıcı. The NAVTEX calls on mariners passing through the area to maintain a safe distance from the vessels carrying out the work. The TRT Haber website writes that the planned natural gas pipeline between Turkey and the  pseudo-state aims to deliver natural gas from Turkey to the island in the future and strengthen the pseudo-state’s security of energy supply. It is maintained that, following the construction of the underwater water-supply pipeline from Turkey to the pseudo-state, the project is considered one of the important steps toward improving energy infrastructure between “the two countries.” The NAVTEX announcement stated that the notice will expire on December 31, 2026.

items.title: Greece’s Electricity Exports Hit New Record
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Despite rising electricity prices internationally and across the region due to the energy crisis, Greece has maintained its competitive advantage over neighboring countries, increasing its electricity exports to the region. According to data from the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO) and the Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT), electricity exports rose sharply in the first eight months of 2026, making a significant positive contribution to the country's trade balance. Net electricity exports (exports minus imports) reached 6.1 terawatt-hours (TWh) between January and August, according to IPTO, and its Chairman and CEO Manos Manousakis told ANA-MPA that, "this development is the result of our national energy strategy to harness our abundant domestic renewable resources, namely solar and wind energy, as well as the systematic development of our electricity infrastructure.”

The post Greece’s Electricity Exports Hit New Record appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Transatlantic ΣΥΝ-ERGIES Highlighted U.S.-Greece Strategic Cooperation
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – The Hellenic-American Chamber of Commerce (HACC), in collaboration with the American College of Greece (ACG) and the American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce (AmCham Greece), hosted ‘Transatlantic ΣΥΝ-ERGIES: Energy, Capital & Global Ventures’ on November 4 at Chiotes Hall in New York City, under the auspices of the Consulate General of Greece in New York. The event brought together distinguished representatives of government, business, academia, energy, finance, and the maritime industry for an evening of substantive dialogue on the evolving U.S.-Greece strategic partnership and the growing importance of energy security, infrastructure development, investment, and technological innovation. The gathering underscored Greece's increasingly significant role as a strategic energy and infrastructure hub connecting the United States, Europe, and the Eastern Mediterranean, while highlighting opportunities to transform transatlantic cooperation into meaningful commercial partnerships.

On the beach in Pamunugama, on Sri Lanka’s west coast, women in uniform work under the scorching sun. They sift through rubbish washed ashore, searching among the usual litter for something much smaller: tiny plastic pellets.

Five years ago, in May 2021, this same beach was swamped with pellets as smoke rose over the Indian Ocean.

items.title: The next global pandemic could be brewing on a mink farm in Utah – and little is being done to stop it | George Monbiot
items.summary_raw:
Mink farms are the perfect petri dishes for deadly flu strains to emerge. Yet officials appear to be protecting business interests over human lives

Could this be ground zero? Could it be the spot where the next pandemic begins? It’s certainly a candidate, not least because the chain of events that could trigger a plague far worse than Covid-19 looks like the opening sequence of a disaster movie. A really bad disaster movie, in which the levels of carelessness and turpitude defy belief.

A report by the investigative news service ProPublica reveals that bird flu has been raging in a mink farm in Utah since August, and it appears next to nothing has been done by public officials. In 2023, I warned in the Guardian that mink farms could scarcely be better designed to generate lethal plagues. This is for three reasons: mink are fed on the offcuts of chickens, cows and other farm animals, in which new viral variants often develop; mink readily host both avian and human flu virus
